categories.name: MCU, Inverter & Motor Hardware Configuration
categories.description: Covers the target MCU board, motor-driver hardware, motor and power-supply configuration, phase connections, current sensing, and hardware PWM outputs.
requirements: The firmware shall target the NUCLEO-G431RB MCU board.
The system shall use the X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 motor-driver board (STSPIN830).
The target motor shall be the GBM2804H-100T gimbal motor with 7 pole pairs.
The system supply shall be 12 V DC.
The firmware shall drive the three-phase motor via U, V, and W outputs to the motor connection.
The firmware shall measure motor phase currents using the X-NUCLEO-IHM16M1 three-shunt current-sensing circuitry.
The firmware shall use MCU hardware PWM generation for the three-phase inverter drive signals.

categories.name: Sensorless FOC & Motor Operating Control
categories.description: Covers sensorless FOC execution, motor state transitions, speed and direction control, startup and stopping behavior, and commissioning of control parameters on the target motor and supply.
requirements: The firmware shall implement sensorless Field-Oriented Control (FOC) for three-phase motor control.
After system initialization, the motor shall remain stopped until a valid START command is received.
The firmware shall support clockwise and counter-clockwise motor rotation as commanded.
The firmware shall allow changing the target speed while the motor is running without requiring a stop.
If a direction change is commanded while the motor is running, the firmware shall perform a controlled deceleration to zero speed before applying torque in the new direction.
If the motor fails to achieve sustained rotation within a bounded startup time or number of attempts from standstill, the firmware shall declare a startup fault and disable PWM.
The system shall achieve reliable motor startup from standstill.
The system shall maintain stable rotation at the commanded speed.
The system shall perform a controlled motor stop when stopping is commanded.
Final speed, startup, and current limits shall be tuned and validated on the actual motor and supply before extended operation.

categories.name: UART Command & Status Interface
categories.description: Covers the UART transport configuration, command parsing and validation, runtime motor commands, malformed-command handling, and formatted system-status responses.
requirements: The firmware shall provide a UART interface configured for 115200 baud, 8 data bits, no parity, 1 stop bit (8-N-1).
Upon receiving "MOTOR START" over UART, the firmware shall start the motor and enter the run state.
Upon receiving "MOTOR STOP" over UART, the firmware shall stop the motor.
Upon receiving "SPEED <RPM>" over UART, the firmware shall set the target speed to the specified value within the allowed range of 300 to 1000 RPM.
Upon receiving "DIR CW" over UART, the firmware shall set the commanded direction to clockwise.
Upon receiving "DIR CCW" over UART, the firmware shall set the commanded direction to counter-clockwise.
The firmware shall implement the STATUS command over UART to report the system status.
The firmware shall ignore unrecognized or malformed UART commands without changing the system state.
The firmware shall reject SPEED commands outside 300–1000 RPM and shall not change the target speed in response.
The STATUS command shall include the current system state.
The STATUS command shall include the target speed.
The STATUS command shall include the estimated actual speed.
The STATUS command shall include the current commanded direction (CW or CCW).
The STATUS command shall include the current fault status.
When a fault is present, the STATUS response shall include a fault code that identifies the fault category (e.g., undervoltage limit, overcurrent limit, sensor fault, startup failure).

categories.name: Drive Safety, Fault Handling & Reset Protection
categories.description: Covers current, voltage, and operating-limit enforcement; phase-sensor and motor-control fault responses; watchdog protection; and safe PWM and motor behavior across faults and MCU resets.
requirements: The firmware shall limit motor current so that RMS current does not exceed 1.5 A RMS or a lower validated project limit.
On detection of a motor-control fault, the firmware shall immediately disable PWM output to the inverter.
The system shall not operate the motor outside the configured voltage and current limits.
The firmware shall prevent motor start and shall stop the motor and disable PWM when the measured DC supply voltage is outside the configured allowable range.
The firmware shall detect loss or out-of-range behavior of phase current measurements (e.g., disconnection, saturation, rail) and immediately disable PWM, entering a fault state.

On any MCU reset, watchdog reset, or brown-out event, the firmware shall ensure PWM outputs are disabled and the motor remains stopped until initialization completes and a valid START command is received.
The firmware shall enable a watchdog that resets the MCU if the control software fails to service it within a configured interval, ensuring fail-safe shutdown of the drive on software hang.
